key_insight: 2D/3D perovskite band alignment is highly sensitive to surface termination, composition, and interfacial polarization, making interface chemistry a key lever for passivation and device performance.
engineering_relevance: These results help guide the design of more stable, high-efficiency perovskite solar cells by showing which interface chemistries are likely to improve moisture resistance without introducing unfavorable band offsets.
method: Hybrid first-principles simulations with optimized hybrid functionals
Computed work function, electron affinity, and band offsets across different surfaces
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preliminary computational results showing work-function shifts, interface-induced macroscopic potential slopes, and band offsets varying by about 0.2–0.7 eV depending on termination and composition.
watch_item: Because the findings are preliminary and based on idealized atomistic models, real-device behavior may differ due to defects, disorder, and fabrication-dependent interface quality.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
